photos.question: A client takes methotrexate once a week for rheumatoid arthritis. Which instruction should the nurse include?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #308!

🍷 Once a week, not once a day. Do you know the big methotrexate rules?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Avoid alcohol while taking this medicine

🧠 Rationale: Methotrexate can damage the liver, and alcohol adds to that risk.

It is taken once a week for RA. Daily dosing by mistake can be fatal.

Folic acid is often given to reduce side effects, and live vaccines are avoided.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Methotrexate

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Antimetabolite, DMARD (disease-modifying drug for RA)

⚠️ Adverse Effects:

🔹 Liver toxicity

🔹 Bone marrow suppression, infection risk

🔹 Mouth sores and nausea

🔹 Harmful in pregnancy

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Take on the SAME day once a week

✅ No alcohol

✅ Keep lab appointments: CBC, liver and kidney tests

✅ Report fever, sore throat or mouth sores

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Metho-TREX-ate for RA: once a WEEK, never every day!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: Which finding suggests chronic venous insufficiency in the legs?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #309!

🦵 Veins or arteries? This leg finding gives it away!

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiovascular question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Brown skin discoloration around the ankles

🧠 Rationale: In venous insufficiency, blood pools in the lower legs.

Red blood cells leak into the tissue and leave brown staining near the ankles.

Shiny hairless skin, weak pulses and pain eased by dangling the legs point to arterial disease.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Venous vs Arterial Disease

🩸 Venous Signs:

🔹 Brown discoloration, swelling

🔹 Warm skin, normal pulses

🔹 Ulcers near the inner ankle

❤️ Arterial Signs:

🔹 Shiny, hairless, cool skin

🔹 Weak or absent pulses

🔹 Ulcers on toes, pain with walking

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Venous: ELEVATE legs, use compression

✅ Arterial: keep legs dependent, no compression

✅ Teach to avoid crossing legs

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Venous = Very swollen, Elevate. Arterial = Away from heart, Dangle.

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #VenousInsufficiency #Cardiac #PVD #MedSurg #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A client with asthma is prescribed montelukast. Which statement shows understanding of the teaching?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #310!

🌬️ Controller or rescue? Students mix this one up all the time!

This is a HIGH-YIELD respiratory question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — "I take it every day, even when I feel fine."

🧠 Rationale: Montelukast is a leukotriene receptor blocker used to prevent asthma symptoms.

It must be taken daily to work, even on good days.

It does not stop a sudden attack. A rescue inhaler like albuterol does that.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Montelukast

💊 Drug Class:

🔹 Leukotriene receptor antagonist (controller)

❤️ Primary Use:

🔹 Long-term asthma control

🔹 Allergic rhinitis

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Headache

🔹 Mood or behavior changes: report right away

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Take once daily, usually in the evening

✅ Keep albuterol for sudden symptoms

✅ Do not stop without talking to the provider

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Montelukast = Maintenance. Albuterol = Attack.

photos.question: The nurse teaches a client how to store insulin at home. Which instruction is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #311!

❄️ Fridge, freezer or counter? Where does insulin belong?

This is a HIGH-YIELD endocrine question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Keep unopened vials in the refrigerator

🧠 Rationale: Unopened insulin is stored in the refrigerator until the expiration date.

An opened vial can stay at room temperature for about 28 days for most types.

Never freeze insulin, and roll cloudy insulin gently instead of shaking it.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Insulin Storage

🧊 Storage:

🔹 Unopened: refrigerator

🔹 In use: room temperature, most types about 28 days

🔹 Never freeze, keep out of heat and sun

⚠️ Discard If:

🔹 It was frozen or overheated

🔹 Clear insulin looks cloudy

🔹 Past the date or open too long

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Write the open date on the vial

✅ Roll NPH gently between hands

✅ Room-temperature insulin stings less

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Fridge to store, room temp to use, freezer NEVER!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

#NCLEX #NursingSchool #NCLEXPrep #Insulin #Diabetes #Endocrine #NursingPharm #NursingStudent #FutureRN #NursingEducation

photos.question: A child has phenylketonuria (PKU). Which item should the parents avoid giving the child?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #312!

🥤 One common diet drink ingredient is a big NO in this condition!

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Diet soda with aspartame

🧠 Rationale: In PKU, the body cannot break down phenylalanine.

Aspartame turns into phenylalanine, so it must be avoided.

High levels can harm brain development, so a low-phenylalanine diet is lifelong.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Phenylketonuria (PKU)

🧬 What It Is:

🔹 Inherited enzyme defect

🔹 Found on the newborn screen

⚠️ Avoid:

🔹 Aspartame

🔹 High-protein foods: meat, eggs, milk, nuts

✅ Allowed:

✅ Special PKU formula

✅ Most fruits and vegetables in planned amounts

✅ Low-protein breads and pastas

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Teach label reading

✅ Monitor phenylalanine levels

✅ Refer to a dietitian

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

PKU = Please Keep Unsweetened by aspartame!

photos.question: A postpartum client who is not immune to rubella receives the MMR vaccine. Which instruction is most important?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #313!

💉 Rubella vaccine after birth: what is the one big teaching point?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Avoid becoming pregnant for 4 weeks

🧠 Rationale: MMR is a live virus vaccine.

It is given after birth when the client is not immune, because it is not given during pregnancy.

Pregnancy should be avoided for 4 weeks. Breastfeeding and newborn contact are safe.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Postpartum Rubella Vaccine

💊 Vaccine Type:

🔹 Live, attenuated MMR (measles, mumps, rubella)

🤰 Why It Matters:

🔹 Rubella in pregnancy can cause birth defects

🔹 Not given during pregnancy

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Avoid pregnancy for 4 weeks

✅ Breastfeeding is safe

✅ Mild rash or joint aches can happen

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Live vaccine = Leave pregnancy plans for 4 weeks.

photos.question: A client is having a panic attack in the dayroom. What should the nurse do first?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #314!

😰 Racing heart, fast breathing, sudden fear. What is your FIRST move?

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: D — Stay with the client and speak calmly

🧠 Rationale: During a panic attack, the client cannot focus or learn new information.

Staying with the client and using short, calm statements gives safety.

Teaching and exploring the cause come later, once anxiety goes down.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Panic Attacks

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Racing heart, chest tightness

🔹 Rapid breathing, dizziness

🔹 Intense fear or feeling of doom

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Stay with the client

✅ Use short, simple, calm words

✅ Move to a quiet, low-stimulus area

✅ Coach slow breathing

📝 Later:

✅ Teach coping skills when calm

✅ Explore triggers together

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Panic = Presence first, Problem-solving later.
